committee.sub: Morning brief · Friday 2 October 2026 · the committee’s read on the 7am numbers

items.text: Spend held steady at $124.68 over the last 7 days for 20 clicks at $6.23 CPC, but conversions are still zero, so cost per lead remains undefined rather than improving.
CTR fell from 4.2% to 2.7% even as impressions rose from 528 to 747, and rank lost (73%) still dwarfs budget lost (22%), so the constraint is ad rank, not spend; the budget conversation stays closed.

The homepage (31 sessions) and /ai-automation-agency.html (16 sessions) are carrying the traffic, but calculator usage dropped to 0 this week from 1 the week before, so almost nobody is reaching the time-cost step.

Organic Search collapsed from 15 sessions to 2, while AI Assistant traffic held at 1 session with chatgpt.com the source, worth watching given it undercounts true AI referral activity; LinkedIn fell to 0 from 1, which may just mean recent links went untagged rather than posting having stopped.

actions.text: Logo and image assets plus keyword-matched RSA headlines for the serving ad groups are still outstanding.
The homepage form confirm-then-count fix is still open: make kontrolTrackLead fire on the Formspree verdict, not before it.
RSA description D1 still claims 13.3 hours of admin per week; update it to match the current site stats.

weekly: a 9% rise, but the gain sits mostly in unexplained Direct traffic (31 vs 10) rather than a channel you can point to.
and calculator use dropped to 0 uses this week from 1 last week, so the funnel's middle step is going quiet.
Paid Search softened to 14 sessions from 20
while Organic Search fell sharply from 15 to 2; AI Assistant traffic held flat at 1 session via chatgpt.com, still the only unpaid growth signal worth tracking.
Search Console data through 28 September (two days behind) shows 173 impressions and 8 clicks over 8 days,
with the top page /simpro-xero-integration.html drawing 60 impressions but zero clicks at position 14.
The homepage and /ai-automation-agency.html remain the only landing pages doing real work,
at 31 and 16 sessions respectively, with everything else in single digits.
